title: First instrument banjo, first band, then saxophone lessons
summary: Banjo was first, taken up in 1925; a year and a half later he joined Paul Moody's band, then studied sax with David Jones.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: No, yeah, banjo before violin. That's right. I took up banjo in 1925. About a year and a half later, I went to work with Paul Moody. You might have heard of Paul Moody. I worked with his band for quite a while. Then I decided I wanted to take up sax. I took lessons from Professor David Jones on the Pelican. He used to be an old Pelican Rampart and Grabby. Then I began to play a little bit. Then I went to work playing sax. The Paul Moody band. Then from there, I went to the quarters. I stayed in the quarters for many years. I worked at a joint called the Last Ronda. On a gamble between Dolphin and whoever. Last Ronda. I must have worked there about six years, six or seven years ago.
